evidence: frontend/apps/admin-web/src/pages/TenantLifecyclePage.tsx — the Restore card (:749-791) presents a fully-built, working-looking feature that does nothing. It renders a descriptive body claiming real capability — `Upload a previously exported tarball into a new tenant slug. Multipart — resumes on disconnect.` (:752-755) — a <FileUpload accept=".tar.gz"> dropzone (:758-775) that even drives a fake progress bar (`progress: isUploading ? 50 : 0` :769), and a primary `Upload` button with a spinner and `Uploading…` state (:778-786). The card is gated behind the real `canRestore` capability (:756), so it is shown to authorized platform admins as a live control, not a disabled placeholder.

The button's onClick is `handleUpload` (:781), whose entire body (:627-640, comment `// Restore upload stub`) is: set isUploading true, then `showToast({ type: 'info', title: 'Upload not yet implemented', message: 'Multipart restore endpoint not yet wired. File selected: ...' })`, then finally reset isUploading. It never calls fetch, the api-client, or any endpoint — contrast the sibling export/purge handlers in the same file which DO call `fetch('/api/v1/admin/tenants/${id}/export|purge')` (:311, :599). So a platform admin selects a backup tarball, sees a spinner + 50% progress bar + an 'Uploading…' label, and gets only an info toast; no tenant restore occurs and no error is raised. The UI actively misleads: the progress bar and button state imply an in-flight upload that does not exist.

This is an incomplete-feature / misleading-UI defect reachable in the production platform-admin console (same class as ppt-web's silent-mutation findings but here the mutation is entirely absent behind a convincing UI). Landable frontend-only remedy without waiting on the backend: make the incomplete state honest — disable the Upload button, drop the fake `progress: 50`, and label the card 'Restore (coming soon)' or hide it behind a feature flag — OR, once the backend multipart-restore endpoint exists, wire handleUpload to it through @ppt/api-client with real progress + error surfacing (reuse the export handler's showToast error pattern :384-397). Verifiable via `pnpm --filter @ppt/admin-web typecheck` + a Vitest/RTL test asserting the Upload button either performs a request or is disabled. Confidence medium: the stub body and its wiring to the visible Upload button are confirmed by static read; production reachability is inferred from the `canRestore` gate, not runtime-confirmed.

frontend/apps/admin-web/src/pages/TenantLifecyclePage.tsx renders its entire UI — including destructive-operation copy — with hardcoded English string literals and never imports react-i18next (grep for `useTranslation` / `t(` over the file returns ZERO hits; it is one of only 5 admin-web page/feature files with no i18n import). Confirmed hardcoded user-facing strings across the page: the picker label `Tenant slug` (:657) and `Load` button (:668/:669); the page header `Lifecycle · {tenant.name}` (:675); card titles `Export` (:689), `Purge · irreversible` (:719), `Restore` (:751); the purge-wizard heading `Purge wizard — proceed carefully` (:351); the MFA prompt `Enter 6-digit authenticator code` (:468); the purge-button labels `Tenant is not soft-deleted yet` / `Cooldown · ... left` / `Purge tenant` (:647-651); and every toast title/message — `Tenant purged` (:324), `MFA required` (:331), `Purge failed (...)` (:336), `Network error` (:341), `Export failed` (:386/:396), `Export started` (:606), `Export failed (...)` (:612).

admin-web is a fully i18n-enabled app: it ships src/i18n/index.ts and sibling admin pages use react-i18next heavily (e.g. OrganizationsPage.tsx has 54 `t('` calls). The 2026-09-20 admin-web review already filed the same i18n-gap class for Dashboard.tsx + OAuthClientsPage.tsx (code-review-admin-web-dashboard-hardcoded-i18n); this is the SAME class on a distinct, higher-stakes page (tenant purge/export/restore) that was never previously flagged. A non-English-locale platform admin performing an irreversible tenant purge sees all confirmation and error copy in English regardless of selected language, which is both an i18n completeness gap and a safety concern for destructive ops.

Landable frontend-only remedy: add `useTranslation()` and move the header/card-title/button/toast strings into the admin-web tenant-lifecycle i18n namespace (mirroring OrganizationsPage). Low severity (+1, i18n gap per the skill's severity table; explicitly not a nit given the destructive-operation context). Verifiable via `pnpm --filter @ppt/admin-web typecheck` + a Vitest asserting a translated key renders. Confidence medium: the hardcoded strings and absent i18n import are confirmed by static read; no runtime locale switch was exercised.
